A market city, and a street at the edge of change

About 500 years ago, Kempegowda I laid out Bangalore as a land of petes (markets), kotes (forts) and keres (lakes). Markets have been part of this city's identity ever since.

Veerapillai Street sits between the bustle of Commercial Street, a residential neighbourhood and an emerging cultural hotspot. It is quieter than its famous neighbour, and it is at the threshold of change. The question is how.

      The exhibition

      Shown to the public at the BDW 2026 Protopolis

      The Designpete concept went on display so people could walk the street, react to the ideas and leave their own. Here is what the room looked like and what visitors told us.

      When
      26 & 27 September 2026
      Where
      Venkatappa Art Gallery, Bengaluru
      What was shown
      A Living City
      Who came
      650 visitors

      Photos from the exhibition

      What visitors told us

      “I walk past these old arcades every day and never really looked at them. Seeing them in the model made me stop.”

      Meera Krishnan, 58

      “Keep the hawkers. Give them better shade and a clean place to store their carts.”

      Ananya Rao, 24

      “A weekend market with music would bring families here.”

      Rahul Menon, 32

      “Please fix the footpath first. Everything else can follow.”

      Arjun Shetty, 41

      “I would love a heritage walk led by people who grew up on this street.”

      Nisha Kapoor, 27

      “Can the same idea work on other streets in the city?”

      Vikram Iyer, 67
